introduction.title: Welcome to JavaScript with Blockly!
introduction.text: Thank you for participating in the testing of this prototype JavaScript learning tool! There are four gamified exercises with different gamification elements scattered around. The focus of the research is on the engagement gamified elements provide in this experience. You can close this dialog and start coding with the blocks.

help.title: How to use Blockly:
help.text: (1) Select blocks from the toolbox on the right and connect them to generate code. (2) Press the evaluate button to attempt clearing the exercise. Check if your code prints something by opening your browser console using 'Ctrl + Shift + J'. (3) You can get more information on what each block does by hovering over them. (4) Right clicking blocks lets you copy and delete them as well. (5) After clearing a level you can switch to earlier one from the menu on top right corner. (6) If an exercise doesn't seem to work, remember to use the variable names mentioned in the exercise description. Extra blocks may also interfere with clearing an exercise so try to remove blocks that are not used.

end.title: Congrats!
end.text: Thank you for participating! This was the last exercise and next we can discuss what you thought of it \(^o^)/

badges.exercise2: Use a for loop for the first time.
badges.exercise4: Make music with note blocks that you get as a reward from Exercise 3.

exercise1.title: Exercise 1 - Hello world!
exercise1.task: This is a tutorial for using Blockly. Print "Hello world!" in the console by dragging and dropping the blocks to the Blockly workspace. Open your browser's console to see if it works by pressing 'Ctrl + Shift + J'. Remember capital letters and the exclamation mark!!

exercise2.title: Exercise 2 - Apple loop
exercise2.task: You have a variable called apples that represents the number of apples you have. You also have ready functions for changing the number of apples. Find out how many apples you have and then change the number to 10 in one go. Try to use the apple functions as little as possible!
exercise2.challenge: Badge: Solve the exercise using a 'count with i' loop block to unlock a new badge!

exercise3.title: Exercise 3 - Age verifier
exercise3.task: Your task is to create a code that asks for the user's age. Create a variable called 'age' to do this and give it the user's age. If the user is under 15, print "Must be at least 15 to access" and print "Welcome" if they are 15 or above.
exercise3.challenge: Reward: Use the 'prompt for text' block to clear the exercise. Type 'How old are you?' as the text prompt and give a number when you run the code.

exercise4.title: Exercise 4 - Lotto numbers
exercise4.task: Create an array called 'lotto numbers' that has seven random numbers from 1 to 40 (the numbers can show up multiple times). Loop through this array using a variable called 'i' and print the lotto numbers to your console. Tip: Blocks can be copied through right click menu.
exercise4.challenge: Bonus: Use note blocks in your code.
